title: Udhayanidhi Stalin Detained by Police After FIR Over Remarks Against CM Vijay and Trisha
excerpt: The DMK leader and Leader of Opposition was taken into custody in Chennai after an FIR was filed over alleged defamatory remarks at a rally, prompting the Madras High Court to agree to urgently hear his anticipatory bail plea.
body:
• DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin was detained by Chennai police on August 4 following an FIR filed over alleged defamatory remarks against Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and actor Trisha Krishnan at a rally the previous day.
  • The Madras High Court has agreed to urgently hear Udhayanidhi's anticipatory bail plea, signalling the political sensitivity of the case.
  • The incident marks a sharp escalation in the DMK-TVK political rivalry, coming weeks after another DMK MLA was arrested for similar remarks targeting CM Vijay.
  • Udhayanidhi Stalin, son of former CM M.K. Stalin, already faces multiple legal proceedings including Supreme Court cases over his 2023 Sanatana Dharma remarks.

Detention Triggers Political Firestorm

Udhayanidhi Stalin, the DMK leader and current Leader of Opposition in the Tamil Nadu Assembly, was detained by police in Chennai on Tuesday after an FIR was registered against him over alleged defamatory remarks made at a party rally on August 3. The remarks reportedly targeted Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and Kollywood actor Trisha Krishnan.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2084515151861207212

The detention is the latest flashpoint in the intensifying political battle between the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), led by actor-turned-politician Vijay who swept to power in the 2026 state elections, and the DMK, which lost power after a decade in office.

Within hours of the detention, Udhayanidhi's legal team approached the Madras High Court seeking anticipatory bail. The court agreed to hear the plea on an urgent basis, underscoring the high-profile nature of the case.

"Joseph Vijay and Kollywood actor Trisha Krishnan."

A Pattern of DMK-TVK Confrontation

The FIR against Udhayanidhi follows a nearly identical episode last month when DMK MLA and former minister Anitha R. Radhakrishnan was arrested after the Madras High Court refused to grant him anticipatory bail in a case involving objectionable remarks against CM Vijay. That arrest triggered widespread protests by DMK workers across Tamil Nadu.

The escalating war of words between the two parties has centred on personal attacks and allegations, with the DMK accusing the TVK government of using state machinery to suppress political dissent. The TVK has countered that no one is above the law and that defamatory speech targeting individuals must face legal consequences.

The controversy has also drawn in Trisha Krishnan, one of South India's most popular actors, who has largely stayed out of the political fray. Her inclusion in the alleged remarks has added a dimension of celebrity politics to an already combustible situation.

Legal Battles Mount for Udhayanidhi

The latest detention adds to Udhayanidhi's growing list of legal challenges. He faces multiple FIRs across states over his September 2023 remarks comparing Sanatana Dharma to diseases like "malaria and dengue" and calling for its "eradication." The Supreme Court has scheduled a hearing on his plea to club those cases for 2026 and has directed that no fresh FIRs be registered without its permission.

Separately, petitions challenging discrepancies in his election affidavit assets were dismissed by the Madras High Court in June, though questions around asset declarations continue to surface.

What It Means for Tamil Nadu Politics

The confrontation between the DMK and TVK is reshaping Tamil Nadu's political landscape. Vijay's rise from cinema to the chief minister's office has disrupted the state's traditional DMK-AIADMK binary, and the DMK appears to be struggling to calibrate its opposition strategy against a popular leader whose fan base remains formidable.

For the Indian diaspora, particularly the large Tamil community abroad, the political upheaval in Tamil Nadu carries personal resonance. The state's political stability has direct implications for investment flows, IT sector growth in Chennai, and cultural institutions that the diaspora maintains close ties with.

The Madras High Court's hearing on the anticipatory bail plea is expected in the coming days and will likely set the tone for how far the TVK government is willing to push legal action against its principal opposition leader.
